layer: resolve one falsifying edge case in the FK Instance prerequisite before any G0 model run
research_question: Can mapping-level identity and declaration-multiset identity represent exact duplicate SQLite FK declarations reproducibly, and can duplicate occurrence ordinals be stably attached to individual PRAGMA groups?
core_hypothesis: Both policies can produce stable identity sets under FK row order and PRAGMA group-ID permutations. Mapping identity merges only exact structural duplicates while preserving multiplicity as separate metadata. Declaration multiset identity creates unique IDs for every valid declaration but cannot guarantee stable group-to-ordinal association for structurally indistinguishable duplicates.
scope_limits: Does not modify or reverse the original FK Instance Gate NO_GO.
Does not select a production identity policy automatically.
Does not authorize Relation-typed G0, model evaluation, or SQL evaluation.
No natural-language role labels, query text, Gold SQL, business-table rows, or human review.

historical_reference.source: g2_fk_instance_quality_20261024_01 full_001 private audit; public aggregate in its report

policies.mapping_identity: Canonical structure hash; exact valid duplicates share one mapping ID and one forward/inverse edge pair; declaration multiplicity is reported separately.
policies.declaration_multiset_identity: Canonical structure hash plus occurrence ordinal; every valid declaration has one unique ID and edge pair; duplicate group-to-ordinal association is measured but not claimed stable.

success_criteria: Full discovers 11 schemas and reproduces 103 raw / 100 valid / 3 invalid declarations; the frozen dev_tables and schema manifest hashes match.
Full rediscovers one exact duplicate valid mapping group with one excess declaration.
Mapping policy merges only exact structural duplicates, keeps distinct mappings separate, records multiplicity, and has unique mapping IDs with paired edges.
Declaration-multiset policy gives 100 distinct valid IDs, paired edges, and ID sets invariant to FK row order and PRAGMA group-ID renumbering.
The analysis explicitly measures whether the declaration ID assigned to an individual indistinguishable PRAGMA group changes under group renumbering.
stop_conditions: Schema read fails, dataset count or FK denominators differ, or frozen input hashes change.
CPU time exceeds 300 seconds or peak RSS exceeds 2 GiB.
Any output path already exists; retain existing data and use a new run ID for any separately registered retry.
